skill.name: engineering-nba-data
skill.description: Helps users extract, transform, and analyze NBA statistics with the nba_api Python library. It covers player, team, game, standings, live, and endpoint reference workflows.
skill.summary: Analyze NBA player, team, game, and live data with nba_api guidance.
skill.author: Emz1998

security_audit.summary: The reviewed findings are overwhelmingly documentation and notebook artifacts: markdown backticks, NBA endpoint URLs, serialized notebook output, generated tables, and example identifiers. No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, destructive behavior, or unauthorized command execution was found, but three oversized response fixtures could not be inspected and remain low-severity manual review items. Static review was capped at 400/564 representative findings; omitted static matches are unconfirmed, so automatic publishing stays disabled until manual review.

remediation.suggestion: Manually review the omitted 164 static analyzer matches or reduce bundled generated/vendor/reference content before enabling automatic publication.

remediation.issue: Oversized response fixture files were not statically scanned.
remediation.suggestion: Manually inspect the large JSON response fixtures or replace them with smaller representative samples before marketplace publication.

remediation.issue: Notebook outputs contain third-party advertising or tracking URLs from rendered content.
remediation.suggestion: Strip saved notebook outputs and keep only source cells needed to explain NBA API usage.

remediation.issue: Documentation includes many generated long lines that resemble obfuscation to scanners.
remediation.suggestion: Wrap generated field lists and endpoint examples across multiple lines to improve auditability.

content.value_statement: NBA data work often requires finding the right endpoint, parameters, and response format. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through nba_api extraction, transformation, and analysis workflows.
actual_capabilities: Find appropriate nba_api endpoints for player, team, game, standings, and live data tasks.
Explain required parameters such as season, league ID, team ID, player ID, and game ID.
Guide conversion of endpoint responses into dictionaries, JSON strings, or pandas DataFrames.
Support static lookup workflows for NBA players and teams.
Help design data pipelines that export NBA results to CSV, JSON, or database tables.
Reference included endpoint documentation and examples for available fields and datasets.
limitations: Requires the nba_api package and working access to NBA data endpoints.
Does not guarantee endpoint availability because NBA services can change or throttle requests.
Does not provide licensed commercial NBA data beyond what the configured API returns.
Large historical pulls may need rate limiting, caching, and manual validation.

use_cases.title: Build a player statistics dataset
use_cases.description: Collect career, season, or game-level player statistics and prepare them for analysis.

use_cases.title: Create team performance reports
use_cases.description: Retrieve team schedules, standings, box scores, and league dashboards for recurring reporting.

use_cases.title: Prototype NBA data pipelines
use_cases.description: Use endpoint guidance to transform NBA API responses into files or database-ready tables.

prompt_templates.title: Find a player ID
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the NBA data skill to find the nba_api workflow for looking up a player ID by full name.

prompt_templates.title: Fetch season game logs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use nba_api to retrieve game logs for a named NBA player in a specific season and return the fields I should validate.

prompt_templates.title: Compare team box scores
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose nba_api endpoints to compare two teams across recent games, then outline a pandas transformation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Design a repeatable pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reliable NBA data pipeline that pulls standings, schedules, and player stats, handles endpoint limits, and exports clean tables.

output_examples.input: Find LeBron James career statistics and prepare them for a notebook analysis.
output_examples.output: A step-by-step plan identifying the player lookup, the career statistics endpoint, required parameters, and recommended DataFrame validation checks.

output_examples.input: Create a daily team standings report.
output: Parameter guidance for season and league values.
A concise export plan for CSV or database storage.

output_examples.input: Explain why my NBA endpoint request returns no rows.
output_examples.output: A troubleshooting checklist covering player IDs, season format, league ID, endpoint availability, headers, proxy settings, and timeout handling.

best_practices: Validate IDs with static player and team lookups before calling endpoint classes.
Cache repeated endpoint responses and respect service limits during large data pulls.
Check response dataset names and columns before building downstream transformations.
anti_patterns: Do not assume every endpoint returns a single DataFrame or the same column layout.
Do not run large historical pulls without retry, timeout, and caching plans.
Do not hardcode player or team IDs without documenting how they were resolved.
